Election day 2024

By: Anina Peens | Commission

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
What are the expectations when South Africans go to the poll this year?

Unique Selling Point:
It is the most important election since the dawn of democracy. What are the hopes of ordinary South Africans?

Summary:
We follow a first time voter and get her experience and hopes. Then we 'follow her ballot' to indicate where the ballot goes after you made your cross.

Further information:
Leah Charles is a second year student at the university of Witwatersrand in Johannesburg. She says she tried to make up her own mind about who to vote for and not be influenced by her peers or social media. Many of her friends decided not to vote as they argue it won't make a difference. We follow Leah on voting day to understand why it makes a difference to her as a young South African who want to stay here and raise her children here. We then follow Leah's ballot and ask, how does Leah's little voice make it all the way to the score board.

Script:


A JOURNEY TO DEMOCRACY

VISUSUALS; LEAH IN BED SEQUENCE
UPSOUND: LEAH CHARLES NO STRAP
00:01:00:06 - 00:01:22:11
LEAH CHARLES
I'm Leah Charles. I'm 19 years old, and it's my first time voting.
00:01:22:16 - 00:01:49:06
I'm quite excited. it's quite an exciting feeling.
00:02:12:16 - 00:02:45:22
The whole experience to feel the vibe and excited to see what happens.
00:04:26:02 - 00:04:48:12
LEAH CHARLES
I love South Africa with all my heart. And I want to make sure that the country that I'm staying in is going to have good health care. That I'm going to have a good upbringing for my future children.

VISUALS
DOOR BELL RINGS
LEAH MEETS CLAIRE AT THE DOOR
INTRO UPSOUNDS
VO
Leah is a second year student at Wits university in Johannesburg.
00:03:28:19 - 00:03:59:05
LEAH CHARLES
I didn't want to be affected by what other people were busy saying to me about what the decisions and feelings were based on parties. So I went and I found a research article or a like a document that was set up by the I e c, and it was just a bunch of statistics about all the parties.
00:05:45:14 - 00:06:07:23
LEAH CHARLES
VISUALS: LET'S GET IN THE CAR WITH LEAH HERE

VO
For Leah it's a joyful journey to become part of the South African democracy.
VISUALS
DRIVING SHOT
00:05:45:14 - 00:06:07:23
LEAH CHARLES
A lot of people thinking I'm just one person.
00:06:07:23 - 00:06:31:13
LEAH CHARLES
Can I really make a change? And why do you think it's important for you to participate in the democratic process? Well, I think, like you say, everyone thinks it's just one vote, but every vote adds up.

UPSOUND: CLAIRE AND LEAH CONVERSATION
VISUALS: LEAH IN THE CUE AND THEN GOING IN TO VOTE AND WE HEAR HER SPEAK ABOVE THE VISUALS WHILE SHE IS VOTING.
00:06:58:16 - 00:07:18:09
CLAIRE:
You're going to make sure that your ballot will be counted properly and it will go to the party that you voted for?
LEAH CHARLES
Well, you do have those stories in your head that have been played or of ballots have gone missing or whatever. But I do I do hope and I do have a feeling that it is going to be counted.
00:07:46:01 - 00:08:06:12
CLAIRE:
Do you know what happens to a ballot after you've put it in the box?
LEAH CHARLES
I know it goes through like a whole chain. I don't know exactly what happens.
VO
It seems, like Leah, most people are unsure of exactly what happens after you put your ballot in the box.
VOXIE 1
I think the votes all get collected and centralised at some point.
VOXIE 2
From here it goes to – I think it’s the national centre, where they open the ballot papers and they do the counting in front of the… er.. The agents and then it goes up onto the big screen.
VO
On the contrary… It will be a mammoth task to sort through piles and piles of votes from over 23 thousand voting stations all under one roof. So votes don't leave the voting station where you voted until each and every one is counted.
00:01:46:19 - 00:02:12:10
MARISKA VAN DER WALT: PRESIDING OFFICER NO STRAP
You see that these demarcations on the floor, the votes will actually not come over this line. So we do not remove any votes from this voting station.
LINK
So when voting day ends the station locks its doors so nobody can leave or enter. Then the seals to these boxes are broken and each vote is counted manually.
VO
When anyone touches a ballot box, the presiding officer, in this case, Mariska van der Walt announces it in the presence of party agents and independent observers.
UPSOUND
VISUALS MARIKSA WITH THE BOX
UPSOUND: There is nothing inside, everyone can see…
VO
When boxes are opened everyone checks that they’re completely empty.
00:03:03:22 - 00:03:27:20
MARISKA VAN DER WALT
00:03:27:22 - 00:03:53:19
“We also check if there is a stamp
00:03:27:22 - 00:03:53:19
“So then face down, we will then be counting votes”
VO
But votes never leave the station but figures are centralized at the national results operation center in Midrand.
LINK
This is the heart of the elections where all the numbers end up. But how does Leah’s vote make it onto that board?
VO
IEC deputy CEO, Mawethu Mosery, explains.
00:03:15:24 - 00:03:44:13
MAWETHU MOSERY
“We've never moved your ballot out of the station, not out of the box. Your vote will be counted”
VO
When counting at the station concludes, the final number is pasted on the door. The ballot boxes are then moved to a provincial office, escorted by police.
00:04:27:22 - 00:05:07:17
MAWETHU MOSERY
When it gets there there would be representatives of political parties who will immediately look at the results. They can compared to a photo that came from their party agents and confirm.
VO
Final numbers are then digitized.
00:05:07:19 - 00:05:40:08
“We do what we call a blind capturing of the results you capture for the first time, it saves and goes and then it forces you to capture again”
VO
And then finally, numbers reflected here, determine our fate.
LEAH
I'm quite nervous, but I'm very excited for what is to come because I do feel like South Africa does maybe need a little bit of a change.

*****

PROMO:

VO: Three ballots, millions of voters and the mammoth task of counting every vote.

UPSOUND:

VO: We follow the ballot in South Africa’s most crucial election.
